title: Normal Americans punished MAGA
gist: Noah Smith reads the 2026 midterm rout — including a Democratic sweep of Texas statewide offices and Trump's base defecting — as a referendum on Trump's tariffs, Iran war and corruption, and as proof that a large non-online 'normie' electorate exists; he warns Democrats against similar overreach and floats AI displacing social media as a depolarizing force.

themes.theme: Scale of the 2026 rout and forecasting misses

insights.claim: Polls, forecasts and prediction markets had called a Democratic midterm victory for months, and the election-night surprise actually broke further toward Democrats, contradicting MAGA's belief in a hidden 'shy Trump' vote.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Polling error in 2026 ran against the GOP, undermining the 'shy Trump voter' prior for future election pricing.
insights.quote: The election night surprise actually favored the Democrats
insights.locator: The MAGA people appear to have

insights.claim: Ron DeSantis projected Democrats would get 55 Senate seats and 250+ House seats and said Republicans are very unlikely to recapture Congress in 2028, possibly not the Senate until 2032.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Implies durable Democratic congressional control and prolonged divided government through at least 2028.
insights.quote: Might not have a shot at Senate control until 2032.

insights.claim: The 2026 Democratic congressional margin was expected to be around 13 points, nearly double 2010's 6.8 points, and above 2008 (10.5) and 2006 (8.0) — the biggest in fifty years.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Magnitude of the swing signals a deep shift in voter sentiment, not a marginal one.
insights.quote: The 2010 margin was 6.8 points, an election remembered as a generational wipeout.

insights.claim: Non-college white voters, Trump's core base, shifted sharply toward Democrats in virtually every state, and young white men went from Trump +28 in 2024 to Democrats +17 per CNN exits.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Erosion of Trump's core coalition reduces the GOP's 2028 floor.
insights.quote: Democrats won young white men tonight by 17 points, per CNN exits

insights.claim: Smith's gut is that Trump will not try to overturn the result via emergency powers, partly because losing young white men makes any street confrontation after an autogolpe unwinnable for MAGA.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Lowers tail risk of constitutional crisis after the midterms.
insights.quote: But my gut says that he won’t

insights.claim: Democrats flipped or led Senate races in Kansas, South Carolina, Iowa and Texas, with Mississippi possibly following.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Red-state realignment broadens Democratic structural power in the Senate.

insights.claim: In Texas, GOP Governor Greg Abbott lost to progressive Gina Hinojosa, James Talarico won a Senate seat, and Ted Cruz is now the only Republican holding statewide office — which Smith calls an epochal, era-defining event.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: A Democratic Texas governor changes the policy backdrop for the state's energy, regulatory and business environment.
insights.quote: The fall of Red Texas is an epochal, era-defining event.

insights.claim: Smith attributes part of the Texas loss to MAGA primary voters replacing popular Senator John Cornyn with Ken Paxton, who has been repeatedly indicted and investigated for corruption, but notes even popular Abbott lost.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Loyalty-driven primaries produce weaker GOP general-election candidates.

themes.theme: Why voters turned on Trump: costs, war and corruption

insights.claim: Smith frames the wave as a referendum on Trump, who is among the least popular presidents in living memory, rivaled only by late-term George W. Bush.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Presidential unpopularity of this scale constrains the administration's policy agenda for its remaining term.
insights.quote: The only possible interpretation of this huge wave election is that it was a referendum on Donald Trump.

insights.claim: Smith argues Trump, elected to tame inflation, raised tariffs on almost everything imported and raised gas prices by attacking Iran, and plunged the US into an expensive Middle East quagmire.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Tariffs and the Iran war are inflationary drivers that shaped voter backlash; watch for any policy reversal.
insights.quote: raised gas prices by attacking Iran
insights.locator: Trump was elected to tame inflation

insights.claim: Reported Trump-linked corruption includes $330 million of donors to the White House ballroom, a $620 million Pentagon loan for a company tied to Donald Trump Jr., and $210.5 million given or pledged to Trump super PACs by companies whose federal cases were dropped.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: These are concrete targets for the incoming Democratic congressional oversight agenda.
insights.quote: Companies whose federal cases were dropped under Trump have given or pledged $210.5 million to his super PACs

insights.claim: Crypto.com (written "Crypto,com" in the source) gave $37 million to Trump super PACs after the SEC dropped an investigation, and Gemini gave $20 million plus $10 million each from founders, per a Public Citizen report.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Crypto firms' political payments and dropped SEC cases are exposed to reversal or investigation under a Democratic Congress.
insights.quote: Crypto,com: $37 million, after the SEC dropped an investigation

insights.claim: The Trump administration's government equity portfolio reached 34 deals, per a Cato Institute tally.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: State equity stakes in private companies are a growing policy channel; affected firms face political risk.
insights.quote: Trump Administration's Equity Portfolio Reaches 34 Deals

insights.claim: A cited report claims US energy executives resigned after the Trump family was caught expediting $25 billion from a sanctioned Russian energy giant in exchange for letting Russians obtain an Alaska natural gas project.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Alaska LNG and Russia-linked energy deals carry sanctions and political risk.
insights.locator: US energy company execs have resigned

insights.claim: Pre-election polls showed corruption topped voter concerns: Fox News found 60% extremely concerned about corruption, WaPo-ABC-Ipsos found about two-thirds think Trump is enriching himself (up 10 points since September 2025), and Reuters/Ipsos found nearly 7 in 10 believe his businesses influence decisions.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Corruption has overtaken prices as the top issue, shaping 2027-28 political priorities.
insights.quote: Voters are now more concerned about government corruption than any other issue

themes.theme: MAGA's echo-chamber delusion and the 'normie' electorate

insights.claim: Smith's core thesis is that MAGA mistook the online right on X for the average American, while normal swing voters who don't care about culture-war memes do exist in large numbers and will punish extremism when pushed hard enough.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Online sentiment is a poor proxy for the median voter; discount social-media-driven political narratives.
insights.quote: the idea that the average American sees things similarly to the rightists on X

insights.claim: Smith contrarianly rejects the long-held claim that swing voters don't exist and elections are won purely by base mobilization.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: A volatile median voter means larger, faster electoral swings than polarization models assume.

themes.theme: Risks for Democrats and the AI/social-media angle

insights.claim: Smith warns that Democrats risk repeating MAGA's error by overreaching — borrowing heavily for health care (raising interest rates and prices), price controls, billionaire taxes, or loose asylum policy — which would bring a red wave in 2030 or 2034.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Watch for a Democratic borrowing binge as a driver of higher rates and inflation if they win in 2028.
insights.quote: They might embark on a borrowing binge in order to throw more money at health care, resulting in rising interest rates and rising prices.

insights.claim: Even as Democrats won broadly, leftist ballot measures failed: California's billionaire tax failed, Washington passed transgender school-sports restrictions, and voters backed tougher fentanyl penalties.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: The wave was center-left, not progressive; policy risk from far-left measures is lower than the headline suggests.
insights.quote: Today's results are better understood as a left-center wave, not a woke one.

insights.claim: Joe Weisenthal hypothesizes 2026 was the first election where social media use fell, with people talking to AI instead, coinciding with moderates overperforming in both parties; Smith finds this consistent with his view that AI partly remedies social media's polarizing effect.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: If AI chatbots displace social media as information sources, political polarization and online-driven narratives could weaken.
insights.quote: The first post-social media election also happened to be the first election in years where moderates in both parties overperformed.
